parsed.summary: Two results are formalized. (1) There is a universal c>0 such that for every finite game G with nonempty answer sets and ε = 1−ω*(G) > 0, and every n≥1, ω*(G^n) ≤ exp(−c·ε^13/(ε+log(|A||B|))·n). (2) For every finite game with ω*(G)<1 there are c,C>0 with ω*(G^n) ≤ C·exp(−cn) for all n. Here ω* is the supremum over finite-dimensional tensor-product strategies with mixed states and POVMs. The main caveat is minor: (2) allows a multiplicative constant C, so it is formally weaker than the conjecture's exact form exp(−c_G n). Since ω*(G^n) ≤ ω*(G) < 1, the two forms are mathematically equivalent, and (1) implies the paper's form anyway.

glossary.plain: Finite two-player game: a probability distribution μ on X×Y and a predicate V(x,y,a,b).
G^{⊗n}: product distribution μ^n; the players win iff V holds in every coordinate.
Family of PSD effects summing to the identity.
Finite-dimensional systems for Alice and Bob, a joint mixed state on A⊗B, and question-dependent POVMs for each player.
glossary.note: Excludes commuting-operator strategies; this is standard for ω*.

glossary.plain: Σ_{x,y} μ(x,y) Σ_{a,b} [V] Re tr(ρ (A^x_a ⊗ B^y_b)).
Supremum of winProbability over all strategies.
glossary.note: Bounded by 1, so sSup is meaningful. If an answer set is empty, no strategy exists and the value is junk 0, which is harmless here.
Includes the constant C; the conjecture uses C=1 for n≥1. The two are equivalent given ω*(G^n) ≤ ω*(G) < 1.

lean_claims.plain: ∃ c>0 such that for all finite X,Y,A,B (in Type) and every game G: if A and B are nonempty and 1−ω*(G) > 0, then for all n ≥ 1, ω*(G^n) ≤ exp(−c·(ε^13/(ε+ln(|A||B|)))·n), where ε = 1−ω*(G).
For every finite game G, ω*(G) < 1 implies ∃ c>0, C>0 with ω*(G^n) ≤ C e^{−cn} for all n ∈ ℕ.

paper_claims.plain: ∃ universal c_qs>0: for every finite game with nonempty answer alphabets, ε = 1−ω*(G) > 0, and every n≥1, ω*(G^{⊗n}) ≤ exp(−c_qs ε^13/(ε+log(|A||B|)) n).
For every finite game with ω*(G)<1, ∃ c_G>0 with ω*(G^{⊗n}) ≤ exp(−c_G n) for all n≥1.

flags.explanation: The bound C·exp(−cn) with arbitrary C>0 is formally weaker than exp(−c_G n) for n≥1. It is recoverable because ω*(G^n) ≤ ω*(G) < 1. Theorem 1.1 is formalized separately in exact form.

lint_verdicts.why: Win probabilities are bounded by 1. The set is nonempty when A and B are nonempty; when it is empty the value is 0, which yields only trivially true instances.
The subtraction is in ℝ, not ℕ.
The denominator ε + log(|A||B|) ≥ ε > 0 because A and B are nonempty.
The argument |A||B| is ≥ 1 by the Nonempty hypotheses, so the log is ≥ 0 and genuine.
A is a Fintype assumed nonempty, so its card is ≥ 1.
B is a Fintype assumed nonempty, so its card is ≥ 1.
